source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.habit: Perennial 0.3–0.6 m tall arising from thick woody root
morphology_source_reported.leaves: One pair of leaflets per leaf, pubescent; lanceolate leaflets 7–12 mm wide [key]
morphology_source_reported.flowers: 2–5 per peduncle [key]; upper 3 stamens much reduced
morphology_source_reported.diagnostics: One pair of leaflets distinguishes from most Senna; wider leaflets and clustered flowers distinguish from S. pumilio

cautions: Flora reports potential livestock toxicity; no independent validation of toxicology
Historical taxon concept requires reconciliation before identification-scoring use
Regional habitat does not establish local BONAP nativity
